title: How to Win My Heart

location.name: Corner Cafe at the Harbor of the Heavens (Inner Harbor)
location.kind: harbor-front corner cafe with a window table, and the harbor promenade around it
location.real_analog: a corner cafe on Thames Street, Fells Point, Baltimore: cobblestones, piers and church steeples on the harbor
near: the new temple across or along the harbor
Atlantis skyline across the water (visible when it hazes)

situation: In daylight the POET walks from the new temple around the harbor to a corner cafe and sits alone, watching romantic couples at other tables. His wishes and losses play as cutaways (a couple at water on Jupiter's moon, an old couple praying in church, flower fields harvested into his power). He keeps watching from a distant window, then stands and walks the harbor as haze rises off the water.
weather_light: bright sunlight on the water; calm; haze begins gathering over the harbor at the end

set_pieces.name: Walk from the temple around the harbor
set_pieces.what_happens: The POET wanders alone from the new temple along the harbor to the cafe.
lines: with every pulsing beat after walking alone
set_pieces.camera: long lens lateral track along the promenade, water and boats between camera and POET
set_pieces.position: harbor promenade between the temple and the cafe

set_pieces.name: The corner cafe table
set_pieces.what_happens: He sits at a corner table and observes couples at other tables, wanting to be noticed.
lines: I want you to notice me in a corner cafe
at the Harbor of the Heavens, wandering in thought
set_pieces.camera: static medium on the POET at the corner table, couples soft in the foreground; eyeline cuts to the tables
set_pieces.position: corner table by the window inside the cafe

set_pieces.name: Distances, younger selves, praying elders
set_pieces.what_happens: Cutaways: silhouettes on opposite shores, ghost children behind glass, an old couple praying together at church.
lines: with the distances we couldn't avoid
our younger selves watching and dreaming
while our elders clutch their pearls
set_pieces.camera: reflections in the cafe window double his face with the ghost children; quiet wide in a church pew for the elders
set_pieces.position: window glass of the cafe; an old harbor church (cutaway)

set_pieces.name: Victory-less seasons (inner montage)
set_pieces.what_happens: From his seat: a lone traveler, burning diary, love letters blown away, dusty trophy cases, flowers frozen in ice.
lines: I've journeyed beyond any place you can conceivably be
life has burned all of my love stories
victory-less seasons for a man that wanted just one win
set_pieces.camera: push in on his still face, then match-cuts into the montage

set_pieces.name: Harvesting the poppies
set_pieces.what_happens: Fields of scarlet poppies and purple blossoms are harvested and become the POET's power.
lines: than the scarlet poppies and purple blossoms
set_pieces.camera: aerial over flower fields; light flowing into his chest in a close-up

set_pieces.name: From a distant window
set_pieces.what_happens: Still at the cafe watching couples; hope that someone will notice him and meet his eyes.
lines: Yet from a distant window, beautiful and calm
hope tells me you'll see me
capture my eyes as you refocus yours
set_pieces.camera: through-the-glass shot from outside the cafe; rack focus from reflection to his eyes; iris close-up
set_pieces.position: the cafe window seen from the harbor

set_pieces.name: Stands and walks the harbor
set_pieces.what_happens: He leaves the cafe and walks around the harbor as haze starts to gather on the water.
lines: all the fatigue of wandering alone in thought
won't prevent me from sharing a smile worth the promise of my heart
set_pieces.camera: follow from behind along the waterline; widen as haze rises off the water

arrival.from_previous: Daytime: the POET wanders from the new temple around the harbor to the cafe.

departure.to_next: Haze gathers on the water and grows; Atlantis, the new temple and the harbor dissolve into haze, which envelops the POET from the ground up while he resists.

encoding: After the brotherhood of the temple the POET goes out into public, to the harbor, to risk being seen by a lover; the cafe window is the film's frame of watching without being watched. The poem names its own place, the 'Harbor of the Heavens', which links the hometown Inner Harbor to the sacred temple: home is now somewhere a heart could be won. It is also the last solid ground before everything turns to haze.
